title: Mount project NAS and enable workbench HDF5 upload
goal: Mount the project NAS NFS export at /mnt/nas on this workstation, then enable the existing Robot Capture HDF5 upload path to /mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw without changing capture, recording, or upload code semantics.
doneWhen: An absent NAS fails closed instead of being replaced by a local directory write
/mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw is writable by the workbench user and a probe file round-trips
config/workbench.yaml upload is enabled with transport=local, remote_raw_dir=/mnt/nas/forge/franka/raw, robot_name=franka-pico
Upload sink probe and offline upload tests pass; remaining unvalidated items are reported
decisions: Mount uses systemd automount + _netdev + nofail so boot never blocks and access to an absent NAS fails instead of writing into an empty local /mnt/nas
Soft NFS timeouts preferred over hard so the long-running workbench cannot wedge in uninterruptible IO; upload already verifies remote size after transfer and retries
Only workbench upload configuration changes; app/upload.py, sink_health.py, recorder and capture code stay untouched
Forge-side franka adapter support is out of scope for this task
NFS version order is vers=4.1 then 4 then 3; the NAS advertises NFS v4 only through rpcbind, so v4.2 was rejected as an incorrect mount option

verification.summary: Local preparation and fail-closed behaviour verified; the mount itself cannot succeed until the NAS export allow-list admits this client (192.168.10.158).
checks: 192.168.10.35 reachable and serving NFS v3+v4 on tcp/2049; export /volume1/robo-data-warehouse allows only 192.168.10.33/.34/.36/.37
mount attempts vers=4.1 rejected (incorrect mount option), vers=4 and vers=3 fail with 'access denied by server'
/etc/fstab unchanged and /mnt/nas left empty so nothing can silently write to local disk
probe_sink with the new config fails closed: Permission denied on /mnt/nas/forge, upload refused
limitations: No real file has been transferred to the NAS yet; rsync/size-verification path unexercised on this rig
Workbench process was not restarted, so the running instance still has upload disabled
Robot Forge has no confirmed franka adapter; only raw HDF5 delivery is in scope here
This host takes 192.168.10.158 by DHCP, so an IP-based NAS allow-list entry is not stable across leases

blocker: NAS export /volume1/robo-data-warehouse on 192.168.10.35 only allows NFS clients 192.168.10.33/.34/.36/.37. This workstation is 192.168.10.158 (DHCP), so mount returns 'access denied by server'. A NAS administrator must add this client (or the 192.168.10.0/24 subnet) with read/write, then re-run scripts/setup_nas_mount.sh.
nextAction: After NAS allow-list is updated: run `sudo bash scripts/setup_nas_mount.sh`, verify write access as embody, then restart the workbench to activate upload and check the UI upload status.
